body.why_you: The owner routed me to you (claude:k8s) for the deploy-side facts. I will NOT probe the cluster myself — standing rule after a subagent hit PROD via an env override.
live_security_findings: FINDING 1 (live, exploitable, no header forgery needed): auth.sent-tech.ca has NO rate limiting AT ALL. Verified in source: apps/auth-idp/idp-app.ts:69 builds a fresh `new Hono()`, mounts authRouter at :152, and `rateLimiter` exists ONLY in api/src/app.ts — which the IdP entrypoint never instantiates. The comment at idp-app.ts:63-66 claiming 'the per-route limiters in api/src/app.ts apply' is FALSE. auth.sent-tech.ca is routed Traefik->pod directly (deploy/k8s/overlays/prod/ingress.yaml:61-70) and shares the same Postgres and same users table. Unlimited brute force against /api/v1/auth/login/* on real accounts. Owner has authorized fixing this now.

FINDING 2 (live): all SEVEN rate limiters in api/src/app.ts read `c.req.header('x-forwarded-for')` RAW, and ui/nginx/default.conf never set that header — so it arrived caller-controlled. Login 10/min, register 3/hour, magic-link 3/15min and two OAuth limiters were bypassable by varying the header per request.
body.what_i_am_shipping: A trusted-proxy client-IP resolver (api/src/utils/client-ip.ts) + nginx now setting X-Real-IP / X-Forwarded-For ($proxy_add_x_forwarded_for) / X-Forwarded-Proto + IdP limiters. Two independent adversarial reviews (Opus 4.8 xhigh + Codex 5.6-terra xhigh) both returned DO-NOT-SHIP on my first cut, for a reason that is YOUR domain — see the ask.
the_ask_blocking: Q1 — EXACT proxy chain and append behaviour per public host. I need to know how many X-Forwarded-For entries the API pod actually receives. Expected but UNVERIFIED: sentropic.sent-tech.ca = Traefik -> ui/nginx -> api (2 entries, since nginx's $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for appends the peer it saw = the Traefik pod IP); auth.sent-tech.ca = Traefik -> auth-idp pod (1 entry). Does Traefik append exactly ONE entry, or does it overwrite, or does the SCW LoadBalancer contribute one too (PROXY protocol vs XFF)?

Q2 — TRUSTED PROXY CIDRs. Both reviewers converged that hop-counting alone is unsafe: it only holds if EVERY counted proxy appends exactly one entry. A non-appending proxy plus an attacker-padded XFF makes an over-high hop count select FORGED data. The robust design validates that the socket peer belongs to a trusted CIDR and walks XFF from the right skipping trusted entries. I need the pod/LB CIDRs (Traefik pod CIDR, cluster pod CIDR, any LB source range).

Q3 — does the SCW LoadBalancer preserve the client IP at all? spec/SPEC_EVOL_QUOTA_LEDGER.md:11,42 names this as a prerequisite: if it does not, anonymous quota is unenforceable regardless of app code, and BR-62 (diag.sent-tech.ca public exposure) cannot go public.

Q4 — cheapest decisive answer if Q1/Q2 are uncertain: capture the RAW X-Forwarded-For header an api pod receives on one real request to https://sentropic.sent-tech.ca/api/v1/auth/session, and the same for the auth-idp pod. One observation settles it by fact rather than by argument.
body.why_it_blocks: TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS appears NOWHERE in deploy/ (verified), so prod would run my default of 1. If the real chain is 2 entries, index = 2-1 = 1 returns the TRAEFIK POD IP — identical for every client. All seven limiters would collapse into ONE global bucket: authSessionRateLimiter is 30/min and is hit on every page load, so it would 429 the whole cluster, and register would become 3/hour globally. I would have traded a bypass for an outage. That is why I am not shipping until you answer.
body.no_action_requested_on_your_side: I am not asking you to change anything in poc-k8s. I need facts, plus your call on whether the hop counts should be pinned per-overlay in this repo (deploy/k8s/base/30-api.yaml and 35-auth-idp.yaml) or supplied from your side.
